description: Use this slot to specify the body part affected by a Condition. This is best used only when the Condition could occur in multiple locations on the body and is not otherwise specified. For example, an instance of lung cancer Condition does not need to specify that the affected body site is the lung. The value in this slot can be any CURIE from Uberon.
Use this slot to specify the age of the Participant when the Condition ended. Only use this slot if the Participant had the Condition at one time, but no longer. Age might be given in days or years.
Example source variable description: AGE WHEN ASTHMA STOPPED|Asthma: If you no longer have asthma at what age did it stop

description: Use this slot to specify the age of the Participant when the Condition started or was first diagnosed. Only use this if the age at Condition start is different from the age of the Participant at the time of the Condition report. Often this will take the form of a separate variable where the Participant is asked how old they were when the Condition started. If the Participant has never had the Condition, this slot should be empty. Sometimes the age will need to be calculated using multiple variables. For example, by adding the age at enrollment and the number of days between enrollment and a Condition diagnosis. Age might be given in days or years.
Example source variable description: Q4d1. Stroke or cerebrovascular age at diagnosis [Neurological History Form. NHX]|AGE WHEN ASTHMA STARTED|AGE WHEN EMPHYSEMA STARTED|AGE WHEN CHRONIC BRONCHITIS STARTED|Asthma: At about what age did asthma start|Q9b. Age first told you had chronic lung disease? [Visit 1] [Personal and Family Health History Form, PFH]|Age first told had diabetes|Days enrollment to F33 Pulmonary Embolism|Days enrollment to PAD

description: This is the slot used to anchor the Condition instance in time. This value is the same as age at visit, age at adjudication, or age at review. This slot was created to accommodate temporal information for Condition instances that are not associated with a Visit (such as those from adjudication).
Example source variable description: Age at visit 1 [Cohort Visit Derived Variables. Visit 1]

description: Use this slot to link a Procedure, MeasurementObservation, Assay, or File to a Condition that is supported by a study record. Sometimes there might be a study record mentioned, but the data not provided. Under these circumstances, this slot should link to a generic instance. If there is associated evidence, the condition provenance should be STUDY_RECORD. Generic forms, quesionnaires, and medical history should not be recorded as associated evidence, but a specific, published questionnaire, such as the Rose Questionnaire, should be recorded as associated evidence. If a variable description indicates that the Condition instance was created based on a study record, then the slot should contain the identifier for that particular Procedure, MeasurementObservation, Assay, File, or QuestionnaireResponse. This information might be contained in the data set description or the study documentation and not at all in the variable desciption.
Example source variable description: Atrial fibrillation flag [ECG data. Visit 4]|BMI WHO grade 3 overweight (BMI >= 30)|ECG LEFT VENTRICULAR HYPERTROPHY|ANGINA BY ROSE QUESTIONNAIRE

description: This is the slot that links the Condition instance to a Participant. This Participant identifier is often in the same table as the Condition variable.
Example source variable description: De-identified ARIC subject ID|SHARE ID NUMBER|WHI dbGaP Subject ID

description: This is the slot that links the Condition instance to a specific visit, where applicable. This is not required. These are usually described as a Visit or an Exam and they are numbered in chronological order. This information can be contained in the variable description or in a separate variable.
Example source variable description: Atrial fibrillation  [Atrial Fibrillation. ATRFIB21. Visit 2]|Self-Report Atrial Fibrillation by the End of V7 [Cohort Status Derived Variables. STATUS71. Visit 7]|Exam number|VISIT

description: This slot will always have a CURIE from either Mondo or HPO (preferably Mondo). See the Condition Concepts table for information on how to assign the proper CURIE.

Use this slot to capture the provenance of the Condition instance. The value in this slot should be one of the ProvenanceEnum. This information can be found in the source variable description, in the data set description, or in another variable.

Use this value in the provenance slot when the Condition instance results from a Participant informing the investigators of their own condition status. This information often comes from a medical history form or questionnaire.
Example source variable description: Self-Report Atrial Fibrillation by the End of V7 [Cohort Status Derived Variables. STATUS71. Visit 7]|HAS/HAD VALVULAR HEART DISEASE?|EMPHYSEMA: SELF-REPORT|Cardiovascular disease ever|[Medical care]. Heart attack? Q8i [Personal History Form, PHXA04. Visit 3]

description: Use this value in the provenance slot when the Condition instance results from a Participant informing the investigators that a doctor or other medical professional told them they had the condition.
Example source variable description: [Medical history]. Have you ever been told by a physician that you had a stroke, slight stroke, transient ischemic attack or transient ischemic attack [TIA]? Q1 [TIA/Stroke. TIAB03. Visit 1]|Emphysema diagnosed by a health professional reported

description: Use this value in the provenance slot when the Condition instance results from a physician adjudication. A physician adjudication is a group of third party clinican experts that review Participant data and make a determination about Condition status. This is very different from an event review. The information indicating that the Condition was the result of a physician adjudication might be in the data set description rather than in the variable description.
Example source variable description: ENDPT - ASTHMA|PERIPHERAL ARTERIAL DISEASE ENDPNT

description: Use this value in the provenance slot when the Condition instance results from information gathered from a third party. This often happens when the Participant cannot speak for themselves.
Example source variable description: A. History. EVER HAD STROKE Q18 [Informant Interview Form, IFI]

description: Use this value in the provenance slot when the Condition instance results from a death certificate, autopsy, or medical examiner report.
Example source variable description: OTHER HEART DISEASE? Q6E [Coroner /Medical Examiner Form]|MI IN LAST FOUR WEEKS Q15B [Coroner /Medical Examiner Form]|

description: Use this value in the provenance slot when the Condition instance results from data collected by the study. This could be a MeasurementObservation or a Procedure. We may or may not be able to link to the actual study record in the associated evidence slot.
Example source variable description: Atrial fibrillation flag [ECG data. Visit 4]|Myocardial infarction, by Minnesota code [ECG data. Visit 2]|Angina based on: 70% or greater obstruction of any coronary artery on angiography on this admission

description: Use this value in the provenance slot when the Condition instance results from an investigator review of a Participant's study data to make a determination about the Condition. This is very different from a physician adjudication. The information that indicates that the Condition is the result of an event review could be in the data set description rather than in the variable description.
Use this value in the provenance slot when the Condition instance results from a hospitalization or discharge record
Example source variable description: PE BASED ON HOSP DISCHARGE SUMMARY DIAGNOSIS|PAD based on: Amputation of one or more toes or part of the lower extremity because of ischemia or gangrene|Section 3: Medical History. Respiratory. Asthma [Heart Failure Hospital Record Abstraction Form, HFA]|PE BASED ON HOSP DISCHARGE SUMMARY DIAGNOSIS

description: Use this value in the provenance slot when the Condition instance results from a clinical diagnostic impression.
Example source variable description: CLINICAL DIAGNOSTIC IMPRESSION: OTHER HEART DISEASE: MITRAL VALVE DISEASE|CDI-OTHER PERIPHERAL VASCULAR DISEASE

description: Use this value in the provenance slot when the Condition instance results from a Participant taking medications for that Condition
Example source variable description: COPD Med Use - self/scanned (ever COPD by MD diag)

description: Use this slot to capture information about the severity of the Condition, if available.
Example source variable description: BODY EXAMINATION: DEGREE OF OBESITY|F136 TTE LVH
BODY EXAMINATION: DEGREE OF OBESITY: 1=SLIGHT|F136 TTE LVH: Mild
BODY EXAMINATION: DEGREE OF OBESITY: 2=MODERATE|F136 TTE LVH: Moderate
BODY EXAMINATION: DEGREE OF OBESITY: 3=MARKED|F136 TTE LVH: Severe

description: Use this slot to record the status of the Condition instance. If the participant was asked if they have a condition, this slot is analagous to their Yes/No/I don't know answer. The data will usually have an enumerative value where 0 might equal ABSENT and 1 might equal present. Sometimes multiple variables are needed to understand the correct status. For example, if a participant is asked if they have ever had a condition (one variable) and then asked if they still have the condition (another variable).
The condition status is PRESENT if the Participant has the Condition in question at the time of the report.
Example source variable description: The values can vary from present, yes, 1, and much more to indicate the presence of a Condition.

description: The condition status is ABSENT if the Participant has never had the Condition in question at the time of the report.
Example source variable description: The values can vary from absent, no, 0, and much more to indicate the absence of a Condition.

description: The condition status is HISTORICAL if the Participant had the Condition in question before the time of the report, but no longer.
Example source variable description: The values can indicate the previous presence of a condition, but often Participants are asked if they have ever had a Condition and then are asked if they still have a Condition. These data are in two separate variables that should be combined in a single Condition instance.

description: The condition status is UNKNOWN if the Participant reports that they don't know if they have the condition
Example source variable description: The values can vary from unknown, don't know, refuse to answer, and much more to indicate that the Condition status is unknown.

description: Use this slot to record who the condition instance should be attributed to - the participant or a relative of the participant. Sometimes a Participant is asked about their familial medical history and this is how that would be recorded in BDCHM. This information is usually contained in the source variable description.
This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to the Participant. This is the most commonly used value for this slot. This should be the default.

This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to the Participant's mother. The age of the Participant's mother might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.
Example source variable description: Did your natural mother ever have any of the following diseases? Stroke? Q15d [Home Interview. HOM. Visit 1]|Q20a. Did your mother have [or does she have] stroke? [Visit 1] [Personal and Family Health History Form, PFH]

description: This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to the Participant's father. The age of the Participant's father might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.
Example source variable description: Did your natural father ever have any of the following diseases? Stroke? Q23d [Home Interview. HOM. Visit 1]

description: This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to one or more of the Participant's children. The age of the child might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.
Example source variable description: Q41a. Have kids been told they had stroke? [Visit 1] [Personal and Family Health History Form, PFH]|FAMILY HISTORY OF STROKE: CHILDREN

description: This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to one or more of the Participant's blood relatives, but does not specify this one. The age of the relative might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.
Example source variable description: Family History of heart attack|Have any of your first degree blood relatives (parent, sibling, child) had pulmonary hypertension

description: This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to one or more of the Participant's brothers. The age of the Participant's brother might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.

This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to one or more of the Participant's sisters. The age of the Participant's sister might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.

This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to one or more of the Participant's siblings, but does not specify brother or sister. The age of the Participant's siblng might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.
